title: A midterm-driven AI selloff erases record earnings from AMD, Super Micro and Arista
intro: Strong reports from AMD, Super Micro, Arista and Lumentum early in the week were overtaken on Thursday, when election results raised fears of political limits on the data-center buildout and chip stocks posted one of their worst days in years. Memory, substrate and packaging suppliers fell hardest, while the hyperscalers themselves edged higher.
movers_note: Tracked value fell 4.3% from Monday's Nov 2 close to $27.51T at the Nov 6 close (down 5.4% from the Oct 30 close a week earlier); Unimicron (-27.1%), Nan Ya PCB (-26.2%), Ibiden (-23.6%), SK hynix (-23.1%) and Delta Electronics (-22.1%) fell most, while Amazon (+5.6%), Microsoft (+4.6%), Arista (+4.0%), Alphabet (+2.0%) and Equinix (+2.0%) gained most.

items.headline: AI-chip stocks plunge as a Democratic midterm sweep stokes fears of a slower data-center buildout
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell 5.52% into correction territory on Thursday as investors worried the election results would slow the AI data-center buildout. Broadcom dropped 10%, Nvidia 9%, AMD and Micron about 15% at midday, and Nebius about 15%.

items.headline: Post-election backlash puts data-center expansion and AI capex under political scrutiny
items.summary: Thursday's tech selloff erased about $2.5 trillion of market value, and the analysis argues the election results will put AI and data centers on political trial.

items.headline: AMD's data-center revenue nearly doubles to $8.5B on the MI450 launch; Q4 guided to about $17B
items.summary: Third-quarter revenue reached $13.4B, with data-center sales up 97% on EPYC CPUs and the MI450 GPU. AMD said Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle run workloads on its first Helios rack systems, and guided Q4 to about $17B.

items.headline: Super Micro books a record $19.9B quarter and guides fiscal 2027 sales to $72-82B
items.summary: Fiscal Q1 2027 net sales were $19.9B, up from $5.0B a year earlier, at a 12.7% gross margin. Next-quarter sales are guided to $19.5-21.5B.

items.headline: Arista grows revenue 58.5% to about $3.66B and guides Q4 to $3.9-4.0B
items.summary: Arista posted its fastest growth since going public, with revenue up 20.5% from the prior quarter. Its fourth-quarter outlook of $3.9-4.0B points to continued AI networking demand.

items.headline: Lumentum more than doubles revenue to $1.26B and guides next quarter to $1.575-1.625B
items.summary: Fiscal Q1 revenue rose 136.5%, split between $754.2M from components and $508.4M from systems. Lumentum guided non-GAAP operating margin to 45-46% for the coming quarter.

items.headline: HBM-driven memory shortage squeezes phones as Qualcomm guides soft and Arm says supply limits it
items.summary: Memory makers' shift toward HBM left less memory for handsets; Qualcomm's quarterly revenue fell 8% to $10.32B and it expects a flat smartphone market next year. Arm's revenue rose 27% to $1.44B, and its CEO said more supply would allow more growth.
